fullNameCn: 拜占庭皇帝约翰一世·齐米斯凯斯
birthPlaceCn: 拜占庭帝国哈尔西亚农地区
deathPlaceCn: 拜占庭帝国君士坦丁堡

titles.title: Domestic of the Schools of the East

events.label: Became strategos of the Anatolic Theme
events.labelCn: 出任安纳托利亚军区将军
events.note: Romanos II entrusted Tzimiskes with one of the empire's most important military commands.

events.label: Served as Domestic of the Schools under Nikephoros II
events.labelCn: 在尼基弗鲁斯二世统治下出任最高军事统帅
events.note: Tzimiskes was one of Nikephoros Phokas's leading commanders and relatives before falling from favor.

events.label: Led the conspiracy that killed Nikephoros II
events.labelCn: 领导刺杀尼基弗鲁斯二世的政变
events.note: Tzimiskes and his allies entered the palace and murdered Nikephoros II, after which Tzimiskes claimed senior imperial power.

events.label: Was crowned Byzantine emperor
events.note: Patriarch Polyeuktos required Tzimiskes to separate from Theophano and punish participants in the murder before coronation.

events.label: Married Theodora, daughter of Constantine VII
events.labelCn: 迎娶君士坦丁七世之女狄奥多拉
events.note: The marriage directly tied Tzimiskes to the Macedonian dynasty while Basil II and Constantine VIII remained co-emperors.

events.label: Defeated Sviatoslav's Rus' at Dorostolon
events.labelCn: 在多罗斯托隆击败斯维亚托斯拉夫的罗斯军
events.note: After a long siege and repeated fighting on the Danube, Sviatoslav agreed to withdraw, ending the Rus' occupation of Bulgaria.

events.label: Annexed eastern Bulgaria and abolished Boris II's imperial title
events.labelCn: 吞并保加利亚东部并废除鲍里斯二世的皇帝称号
events.note: John celebrated a triumph at Constantinople and treated the eastern Bulgarian territories as annexed, although western Bulgarian resistance survived.

events.label: Led a deep Syrian campaign toward Palestine
events.labelCn: 率军深入叙利亚并逼近巴勒斯坦
events.note: Tzimiskes captured or received submission from important Syrian and coastal cities, extending Byzantine influence far into the Levant.

events.label: Died after returning from the eastern campaign
events.note: John died in Constantinople after illness. Later sources alleged poisoning by Basil Lekapenos, but the accusation cannot be established.

sourceNote: John Skylitzes, A Synopsis of Byzantine History (Cambridge); Leo the Deacon, History; Anthony Kaldellis, Streams of Gold, Rivers of Blood; Oxford Dictionary of Byzantium; Warren Treadgold, A History of the Byzantine State and Society; Wikipedia supplementary chronology.
notes:
John I replaced Nikephoros II as senior emperor but preserved Basil II and Constantine VIII as crowned Macedonian co-emperors. His decisive campaigns against the Rus' and in Syria strengthened the empire before the adult Macedonian brothers inherited effective control in 976.
